title: Standing vs Sitting Time Balance
dataSources: Posture readings (`posture:reading`), symptom logs (`symptom:log`), bathroom visits (`bathroom:visit`), sneeze events (`sneeze:event`).
app: Everyday body-signal logs — posture sensors, symptom and allergy journals, hydration-linked bathroom logs, and quirky personal counters — sent to Splunk HEC via wearables, MQTT, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=posture:reading
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(eval(if(state="standing",duration_min,0))) as standing, sum(eval(if(state="sitting",duration_min,0))) as sitting by _time
| eval standing_pct=round(100*standing/(standing+sitting),1)
| sort - _time
description: Tracks how much of your day you spent standing versus sitting, encouraging you to break up long sits.
value: Long unbroken sitting is a well-known health risk; a daily standing percentage keeps a sit-stand desk honest.
implementation: Ingest desk/posture state into `index=personal`; review standing versus sitting balance.
visualization: Column chart of daily standing percentage.
grandmaExplanation: It tracks how much you stand versus sit each day, nudging you to get up and move more often.
